Meanwhile, `UpdateShardHandler.java` has been updated to utilize these configurations by setting the appropriate parameters from the provided configuration object. The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
if (params.get(PROP_SO_TIMEOUT) != null || params.get(PROP_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT) != null) {
    throw new SolrException(ErrorCode.SERVER_ERROR, "The socket connect and read timeout cannot be set here and must be set");
}
```
Reason:
This code checks if the socket connect and read timeout parameters are set in the `params`. If they are, it throws an exception, preventing the `UpdateShardHandler` from configuring these timeouts. As a result, the timeouts are ignored, leading to the bug.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
HttpClientBuilder builder = setupBuilder(newHttpClientBuilder, params);
```
Reason:
By removing the exception that previously blocked the setting of connection and read timeouts, the patch allows the `params` to be passed to the `setupBuilder` method without throwing an error. This enables the proper configuration of the timeouts, thus fixing the bug.
